title: Filename download bypasses completed-digest status check
reasoning: The ID-based download endpoint refuses non-completed digests, but GET /{filename} only validates the extension and file existence. It looks up the Digest only after recording activity and only to optionally set downloaded_at, so a predictable filename can download an EPUB whose database row is still processing or failed, and can also mark that digest as downloaded before completion. This creates inconsistent behavior between the two download APIs and can expose a generated file during the pipeline window before the digest is marked completed.
reproduction: Create a Digest row with filename='2026-05-18_manual.epub' and status='processing', place that file in settings.output_dir, then request GET /api/digests/2026-05-18_manual.epub with valid auth. The route returns 200 even though GET /api/digests/{id}/download would return 409.
recommendation: Resolve the Digest before serving the file and require it to exist with status == 'completed', matching download_digest_by_id. Return 404 for unknown filenames or 409 for known but incomplete digests before recording activity or downloaded_at.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The local tests found for digest downloads exercise /{digest_id}/download only; there is no test coverage for GET /{filename} or for processing/failed digests through the filename route.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that GET /api/digests/{filename} returns 409 for a processing Digest with an existing EPUB file, returns 404 for an orphan .epub file not tied to a Digest row, and still returns 200 for a completed Digest.
minimumFixScope: app/api/digests.py download_digest plus focused route tests for the filename endpoint.
